Don't know about better but it would work, yes. You're swapping a keyflare giver for another.

Thaïs, Horla, Saya, Clementine, Tawil, Caraboo, ...
There are a number of supports that fit great in any team.
Thaïs gives lots of aliemus and debuffs the enemy. Cara brings huge boons but you don't chose them ( only when they will apply ). Ramona gives you arithmetica discount and draw. Horla comes with passive boost once you leap. Clementine guves strength, keyflare, heal and debuffs.
These are only a few exemples.

In my opinion it's mostly a matter of preference and your own playstyle. You could get the very best team ( if that even exists ) but still fail to progress because you don't know how to use them / don't enjoy their gameplay

And if you're planning long term, two thing to keep in mind 
- 5 teams means you will probably need to spread your strongest units even when they have a great synergy
- you will yet get more awakeners so even your ace team for event will change over time.

I'd say, just don't worry too much and enjoy arc 1, it's a great place to try out all manner of different matchups <:Saya_duel:1513123467917135903>
But yeah, in the end this is only my own opinion. If someone else's suggestion feels right to you, then it simply is right for you

content:
Hello there <:Saya_yum:1513124263291387975> 

For help on specific awakener playstyle, you can ask Ærica ( /char ).

> Ultra
- The first card you play each turn is stored in an inaccessible deck called "ultra space".
- That act of copy is called "leap" on regular ultra and "dimension shuffle" with Arachne.
- You can delete the leftmost card of the ultra space with the "annihilation" action. That frees a slot in your ultra space ( if you played a card you don't want there ) and creates an insight in your hand.
- When the ultra space is full ( all 5 slots ) the turn end will instead give you an extra turn. In the "ultra round" you won't draw from your deck but instead recieve cards in your ultra space.

> Singularity:ultra
- Annihilation puts the copy into your hand instead of an insight ( And Arachne's rouse lets you choose the card to take out instead of the leftmost one in addition to triggering an extra "dimension shuttle" with your next card ).
- The ultra round is not an extra turn but an extension of your turn : shield, delayed effects, arithmetica, prepare, etc all reman in the same state as you left them in the regular turn.

So yeah, you had the basics right <:Saya_key:1513122945885536378>

Hello and welcome aboard <:Saya_yum:1513124263291387975> 

Early in the game, the fight are forgiving enough that you don't need a team with a great synergy so my advice is : pick 2 awakeners you like most, fill the blanks and enjoy the story.
By chapter 3, you should understand enough about the game's mechanics to improve the linup by yourself.

You will evebtually want 5 functionnal teams ( 19 awakeners ) so I suggest starting chapter 3 ( or before if you feel ready ) you try a bit of everything and give each awakener in your dorms a chance to shine.

You will get a lot more over time so maybe don't worry too m7ch about which team would ve perfect for you right now : it will evolve. You can upgrade everyone to lvl 40 without to much effort and lvl 60 if you commit a bit ( awakener level matters *a lot* in this game )

- Murphy:Fauxborn is awesome but quite hard to properly use
- Jenkins and Mouchette are heavy damage-dealer, rather easy to master
- Celeste is a great support which provided a free resurection in case things go wrong

Most impirtant of all : this *is* a game. So the right way to play just might be the funniest way to play <:Saya_duel:1513123467917135903>
